title: Model Risk Manager
description: About the role: Mercury is looking for a Model Risk Manager to help build and operate a practical, risk-based Model Risk Management program as we continue to scale and prepare for life as a regulated bank.  Models support an increasingly broad range of decisions across Mercury, including credit underwriting, portfolio management, fraud prevention, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational processes. This role will provide independent review and effective challenge throughout the model lifecycle while helping Mercury apply governance proportionate to the actual risk of each model. This is a hands-on role for someone who can move comfortably between technical analysis, regulatory expectations, and business context. You will conduct model validations, challenge assumptions and limitations, improve our model inventory and monitoring practices, and work closely with teams across Risk Ops, Data, Engineering, Product, Finance, Compliance, and Internal Audit.  Showing up as a true collaborator, advisor and partner to the business will be key as we continue to build out this function and work towards our collective goals at Mercury. You should be comfortable operating in a fast-moving environment where the objective is not governance for its own sake, but helping Mercury use models safely, responsibly, and effectively. What you’ll do: Perform independent validations and reviews of internally developed and third-party models across areas such as credit, fraud, BSA/AML, CECL, finance, liquidity, pricing, and operational risk. Evaluate each model’s methodology, assumptions, data quality and lineage, implementation, and performance through reviews and testings such as outcomes analysis, benchmarking, back-testing, and sensitivity testing scaled to its risk and materiality. Provide credible and constructive challenges to model developers, owners, and users while maintaining effective working relationships with 1LOD. Assess model risk and materiality based on a model’s inherent risk, purpose, exposure, use, and potential impact. Help maintain a complete and accurate model inventory, including model ownership, risk rating, dependencies, limitations, validation status, monitoring requirements, and open issues. Review ongoing monitoring plans and results, including performance thresholds, overrides, data drift, model changes, and conditions that could make a model no longer fit for purpose. Evaluate vendor models and other third-party analytical products, including available documentation, transparency, performance, limitations, customization, and Mercury’s ability to monitor and control their use. Document validation conclusions clearly, identify issues, recommend proportionate remediation, and track findings through resolution. Support controlled model use when validation cannot be completed before implementation by helping establish appropriate limitations, compensating controls, monitoring, and approvals. Develop clear reporting on model risk, validation coverage, performance concerns, concentrations, dependencies, exceptions, and overdue remediation for management and governance committees. Help improve Mercury’s Model Risk Management Policy, standards, procedures, and templates. Use automation and analytical tools to make model inventory management, testing, monitoring, and reporting more efficient. Partner with Mercury’s Data and AI Governance teams to establish clear boundaries and handoffs between traditional model risk management and the governance of generative AI, agentic AI, and other analytical systems outside the formal model definition. Support regulatory examinations, Internal Audit reviews, and other assurance activities involving model risk. What we’re looking for: 5+ years of relevant experience in model validation, model development,  quantitative risk analytics, or a related discipline within banking, fintech, financial services, or consulting. Bachelor’s degree in Statistics, Mathematics, Physics, Computer Science, Engineering, Financial Engineering or a related field. Master’s degree or PhD is preferred.  Strong knowledge of model risk management principles and current regulatory expectations, including the revised interagency guidance reflected in SR 26-2. Intensive experience validating or developing models in one or more areas such as BSA/AML, fraud, financial forecasting, CECL, capital, liquidity, and credit underwriting, using one or more methodologies such as machine learning (e.g., XGBoost, random forests), scorecards, complex vendor models (e.g., Alloy, Firco), and complex spreadsheet-based models. Proficiency with SQL and Python (from a data analytics lens); comfortable building understanding of models independently of their developers through collecting evidence and data analytics. title: Manager, Lease Operations Accounting
description: CoreWeave is The Essential Cloud for AI™. Built for pioneers by pioneers, CoreWeave delivers a platform of technology, tools, and teams that enables innovators to build and scale AI with confidence. Trusted by leading AI labs, startups, and global enterprises, CoreWeave combines superior infrastructure performance with deep technical expertise to accelerate breakthroughs and turn compute into capability. Founded in 2017, CoreWeave became a publicly traded company (Nasdaq: CRWV) in March 2025. Learn more at  www.coreweave.com . About the Team The Leasing Team sits within CoreWeave’s Corporate Accounting organization and is responsible for the end-to-end accounting of CoreWeave’s growing lease portfolio. Our team partners closely with Lease Administration, Accounts Payable, FP&A, Operations, Treasury, Legal, and Technical Accounting to deliver accurate lease accounting, timely close, and reliable financial reporting under US GAAP. As CoreWeave scales its global infrastructure footprint, this team builds the processes and controls needed to manage lease expenses, balances, and reporting across a complex portfolio. Key Responsibilities: As Manager, Lease Operations Accounting, you will lead a team of senior accountants and own day-to-day accounting operations and close execution for CoreWeave’s lease portfolio. You will review journal entries, reconciliations, accruals, and expense analytics; coordinate billing and accounting issues across teams; and support lease disclosures and audits. This is a hands-on leadership role requiring strong ASC 842 knowledge, sound accounting judgment, and the ability to develop people and scale reliable processes. Lead, mentor, and develop a team of senior accountants focused on lease accounting; set priorities, review workpapers, and coach the team on accuracy, documentation, and timely execution Oversee rent, utility, and other cost accruals, including unbilled charges, vendor confirmations, subsequent-invoice checks, and timely true-ups Review recurring operating and finance lease accounting under ASC 842; partner with Technical Accounting on new leases, modifications, and complex judgments, and translate conclusions into accurate schedules and entries Manage month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close activities for the lease portfolio, including journal entries, reversals, prepaid amortization, and reclassifications Review and substantiate lease-related balance sheet reconciliations, including prepaid rent, deposits, lease payables, accruals, and clearing accounts; investigate aged items and drive resolution Reconcile CoStar reports, NetSuite activity, and supporting workbooks; investigate differences and maintain complete, accurate data through system and process transitions Prepare and review balance sheet and P&L analytics for lease-related accounts, explaining rent, utilities, and othercost variances to FP&A and senior finance stakeholders Partner with Lease Administration, Accounts Payable, Treasury, Legal, and Operations to resolve invoice discrepancies, track contractual credits and deposits, and align accounting with commencement and billing information Drive process improvements and maintain SOX controls, clear review evidence, and repeatable procedures;
